summary.text:
Let me verify the logic against tests.

runA := Demand AND NOT FaultA AND (LeadA OR FaultB)
runB := Demand AND NOT FaultB AND ((NOT LeadA) OR FaultA)

Both faulty: runA false (FaultA), runB false. Good.
LeadA true, healthy both: runA true, runB = Demand AND NOT FaultB AND (false OR false)=false. Good.

Fault fallback: LeadA true, FaultA true, FaultB false: runA false, runB = Demand AND true AND (false OR true)=true. Good. P4: Demand & LeadA & !FaultA -> PumpA. With FaultA true, vacuous. Good.

Test fallback step 3: LeadA true, FaultA true, FaultB false → PumpB true, LeadA stays true. Good.

P5: Demand & !LeadA & !FaultB -> PumpB. With LeadA true it's vacuous. Fine.

But P5 with LeadA false and FaultA true, FaultB false: runB = Demand AND NOT FaultB AND (true OR true) = true. Good.

Both healthy & LeadA false: runA = Demand AND NOT FaultA AND (false OR false) = false; runB true. Good.

Test alternate step 4: Demand falls, episode served → toggle LeadA to false. PumpA false since Demand false. Good.
Step 5: Demand false, no toggle (prevDemand false, completedServed requires prevDemand true). Good.

Test fallback step 2: Demand falls after all-faulted episode (episodeServed false) → no toggle, LeadA true. Good.
Step 3: Demand true, FaultA true, FaultB false → PumpB true, episodeServed true. Step 4: Demand true, faults clear, LeadA true → PumpA true. Note runA true despite prior PumpB. Good; episodeServed stays true. Step 5: Demand false, FaultA true FaultB true, completedServed true → toggle LeadA false. Good.

P1: runA and runB both true? runA requires (LeadA OR FaultB); runB requires ((NOT LeadA) OR FaultA). Both true, e.g., LeadA true, FaultB true, FaultA true... then runA needs NOT FaultA false. Consider LeadA true, FaultB true, FaultA false: runA true, runB = NOT FaultB false. If LeadA false, FaultA true, FaultB true: runA false (FaultA). Both healthy and LeadA... runA requires LeadA true, runB requires LeadA false. So can't both. Case LeadA true, FaultB true, runB requires NOT LeadA false or FaultA. FaultB true blocks runB. So mutual exclusion holds. Good.

Compilation passed. Done.

P6/P7 retained state and toggling exactly once. Good.

Note the requirement about "LeadA is the retained preference" — we don't overwrite LeadA in demand. Good.

Final answer.

One subtlety: P7 says !completedServed -> LeadA <-> qLeadA. Our toggle only on completedServed. Good.

Also toggle happens after computing runA/runB with old LeadA — correct because outputs use pre-state and toggle applies to q[k+1]; observed LeadA at end of scan is toggled. Test step 4 expects LeadA false at that scan. Good.

Also completedServed needs to be true also if pump ran during episode. We used episodeServed flag. Fine.

Edge case: Demand true but all faulted during entire episode then faults recovered while Demand still true, pump runs → episodeServed true, toggles on falling edge. That matches.

Done.

FB_Task interface preserved exactly: inputs Demand, FaultA, FaultB; outputs PumpA, PumpB, LeadA (init TRUE). Retained state: prevDemand, episodeServed; helper vars runA/runB/completedServed.

Logic:
- runA := Demand AND NOT FaultA AND (LeadA OR FaultB)
- runB := Demand AND NOT FaultB AND (NOT LeadA OR FaultA)
  → faulted pumps never run, both-off when no demand, mutual exclusion (no simultaneous run), healthy lead preferred with immediate fallback on fault (fault changes take effect within the same scan/episode).
- completedServed := prevDemand AND NOT Demand AND episodeServed → toggles LeadA exactly once on the falling edge of a served continuous demand episode; an all-faulted episode with no running scan leaves LeadA unchanged (P6/P7). LeadA is never overwritten during demand, so it stays the retained preference rather than a report of the present fallback pump.
- prevDemand updated at end of scan; episodeServed set whenever a pump actually ran during the episode and cleared when Demand is FALSE.

All fixed traces of the "alternate" and "fallback" tests are satisfied by construction (initial scan, held demand, served/unserved falling edges, fault fallback, recovery, and a final served episode that toggles the lead). Note: only compiler verification was performed; no PLC functional tests were executed."}
